source: Lovelock, J.E. (1965) 'A physical basis for life detection experiments', Nature 207(4997), 568-570.
translationStatus: ALL translations below are AI-generated and UNVERIFIED. Students who speak each language verify and correct them as a Unit 0 task; verified entries gain verifiedBy + verifiedDate and the site stops showing the warning flag.

terms.plain: Having only one possible meaning. An unequivocal result cannot be argued about.
terms.note: Lovelock wants a test whose answer nobody can dispute.

terms.plain: From beyond Earth.
Taking Earth as the centre or the standard. A geocentric question assumes other places work like Earth.
terms.note: Lovelock uses this as a criticism. Watch how he turns it into a limitation of other people's experiments.

terms.plain: Describing what you can observe, without claiming to explain the deeper reason why.
terms.note: Lovelock calls his own method this. He is being honest about a limit, not apologising.
terms.flag: Translator warning: this is the PHYSICS sense (describing observations), not the philosophy sense. Machine translators usually pick the philosophy word. Check carefully.

terms.plain: The chemistry of living things.
Not made by living things. Rocks and gases are inorganic.
How spread-out and mixed-up things are. Left alone, everything becomes more mixed up. Life pushes the other way.
terms.note: The most important word in the paper. Lovelock's definition of life turns on it.

terms.plain: A spinning whirlpool of water or air.
terms.note: Lovelock's counter-example: a vortex is orderly too, but it disappears quickly. Life does not.

terms.plain: A settled state. Every reaction that could happen has already happened, and nothing is left to react.
terms.note: A dead planet's atmosphere settles. Earth's has not.

terms.plain: How much a substance still 'wants' to react with what is around it.
A situation that stays the same overall, even though things keep moving through it.
terms.note: Not the same as equilibrium. A river can be in steady state while water keeps flowing.

terms.plain: The opposite of equilibrium. Things that should have reacted together are still sitting side by side.
terms.note: Oxygen and methane in Earth's air. This is Lovelock's biosignature.

terms.plain: Being everywhere at once.
Having no life at all.
terms.flag: Translator warning: here it means 'lifeless planet', NOT 'medically clean' and NOT 'unable to have children'. Machine translators often pick the wrong one.

terms.plain: From the earliest times, before anything else.
How much of something flows onto a surface each second. Solar flux is how much sunlight arrives.
Big enough to notice or measure.
Life starting by itself from non-living matter.
A machine that separates a mixture of gases so each one can be identified.
A machine that weighs molecules to work out what they are.
A long molecule built from many identical small units joined in a chain.
How heavy one molecule is.
A burst of heat given out by a reaction.
Heating two samples side by side and comparing them, to see if one reacts.
Breaking a substance apart using heat, without burning it in oxygen.
A molecule made only of hydrogen and carbon. Petrol and methane are hydrocarbons.
A simple type of hydrocarbon with only single bonds.
Made without any living thing involved.
Balanced for now, but one push away from changing.
A standard pattern showing how often random events happen. Real data that does NOT fit this pattern is a sign something non-random is at work.
